# generate-mqtt

Generate AsyncAPI 3.0 MQTT-specific schemas with topic hierarchies, QoS
configuration, retained messages, Last Will and Testament, and MQTT 5
properties from a Linear issue description.

## When to Use

Invoke this skill when the issue mentions any of:
- MQTT protocol, broker, Mosquitto, HiveMQ, EMQX
- IoT devices, sensors, actuators, telemetry
- Device commands, firmware updates, OTA
- QoS levels, retained messages, Last Will
- Topic hierarchies, wildcard subscriptions
- Device twin, shadow, status reporting
- Edge gateway, constrained devices

## Input

| Field | Source | Required |
|-------|--------|----------|
| `issue.identifier` | Linear issue ID (e.g., `UPT-78`) | ✅ |
| `issue.title` | Linear issue title | ✅ |
| `issue.description` | Full issue body — device types, telemetry data, command flows | ✅ |
| `issue.labels` | Labels array | ✅ |
| `workspace` | Absolute path to workspace root | ✅ |
| `mqtt_version` | `3.1.1` / `5.0` — override auto-detection | optional |

## Output

```
{workspace}/
  mqtt/
    {domain}-mqtt.yaml            # AsyncAPI 3.0 MQTT binding (primary)
    schemas/
      {MessageType}.json          # JSON Schema per message type
    examples/
      {MessageType}.example.json  # Payload examples
```

Every generated file starts with:

```yaml
# Generated by Uptempo for {issue.identifier}: {issue.title}
```

## Procedure

### Step 1 — Parse Issue Context

1. Extract device types, data flows (device→cloud, cloud→device, device→device).
2. Identify telemetry fields, command types, and status transitions.
3. Detect MQTT version:
   | Signal | Version |
   |--------|---------|
   | "User Properties", "Response Topic", "Content Type", "MQTT 5" | 5.0 |
   | No version signals, basic pub/sub | 3.1.1 |
4. Default to **MQTT 5.0** if unspecified (superset of 3.1.1).

### Step 2 — Design Topic Hierarchy

Apply hierarchical topic naming:

```
# Telemetry (device → cloud)
{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/telemetry
{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/telemetry/{sensorType}

# Status (device → cloud, retained)
{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/status

# Commands (cloud → device)
{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/commands/{commandType}
{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/commands/response

# Firmware (cloud → device)
{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/firmware/update
{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/firmware/status

# System / management
$SYS/brokers/{brokerId}/clients/{clientId}/connected
```

Rules:
- Use `/` as level separator — never dots or dashes within a level
- Keep levels ≤ 7 deep for performance
- Reserve `$SYS/` prefix for broker system topics
- Device ID level enables per-device ACL

### Step 3 — Build AsyncAPI 3.0 Document

Produce `{workspace}/mqtt/{domain}-mqtt.yaml`:

```yaml
asyncapi: "3.0.0"
info:
  title: "{domain} MQTT API"
  version: "1.0.0"
  description: "{issue.identifier}: {issue.title}"
  x-generated-by: uptempo
  x-mqtt-version: "5.0"

servers:
  production:
    host: "mqtt.{domain}.com:8883"
    protocol: secure-mqtt
    description: "Production MQTT broker (TLS)"
    security:
      - $ref: "#/components/securitySchemes/mtls"
    bindings:
      mqtt:
        clientId: "{org}-{deviceType}-{deviceId}"
        cleanSession: false
        keepAlive: 60
        lastWill:
          topic: "{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/status"
          qos: 1
          retain: true
          message: '{"status":"offline","timestamp":"{ISO8601}"}'

channels:
  deviceTelemetry:
    address: "{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/telemetry"
    messages:
      telemetryMessage:
        $ref: "#/components/messages/TelemetryMessage"
    bindings:
      mqtt:
        qos: 0
        retain: false

  deviceStatus:
    address: "{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/status"
    messages:
      statusMessage:
        $ref: "#/components/messages/StatusMessage"
    bindings:
      mqtt:
        qos: 1
        retain: true

  deviceCommand:
    address: "{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/commands/{commandType}"
    messages:
      commandMessage:
        $ref: "#/components/messages/CommandMessage"
    bindings:
      mqtt:
        qos: 2
        retain: false

operations:
  publishTelemetry:
    action: send
    channel:
      $ref: "#/channels/deviceTelemetry"
    messages:
      - $ref: "#/channels/deviceTelemetry/messages/telemetryMessage"
    bindings:
      mqtt:
        retain: false

  subscribeStatus:
    action: receive
    channel:
      $ref: "#/channels/deviceStatus"
    bindings:
      mqtt:
        qos: 1

  sendCommand:
    action: send
    channel:
      $ref: "#/channels/deviceCommand"
    bindings:
      mqtt:
        qos: 2

components:
  messages:
    TelemetryMessage:
      name: TelemetryMessage
      contentType: application/json
      payload:
        $ref: "#/components/schemas/TelemetryPayload"
      bindings:
        mqtt:
          x-mqtt5-properties:
            contentType: "application/json"
            messageExpiryInterval: 3600
            userProperties:
              deviceType: "{deviceType}"
              firmwareVersion: "{version}"

    StatusMessage:
      name: StatusMessage
      contentType: application/json
      payload:
        $ref: "#/components/schemas/DeviceStatus"

    CommandMessage:
      name: CommandMessage
      contentType: application/json
      payload:
        $ref: "#/components/schemas/DeviceCommand"
      bindings:
        mqtt:
          x-mqtt5-properties:
            responseTopic: "{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/commands/response"
            correlationData: "{requestId}"

  schemas:
    TelemetryPayload:
      type: object
      required: [deviceId, timestamp, readings]
      properties:
        deviceId: { type: string }
        timestamp: { type: string, format: date-time }
        readings:
          type: object
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
      additionalProperties: false

    DeviceStatus:
      type: object
      required: [status, timestamp]
      properties:
        status:
          type: string
          enum: [online, offline, error, maintenance]
        timestamp: { type: string, format: date-time }
        firmwareVersion: { type: string, pattern: "^\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+$" }
        lastError: { type: string, nullable: true }

    DeviceCommand:
      type: object
      required: [commandId, type, timestamp]
      properties:
        commandId: { type: string, format: uuid }
        type: { type: string }
        timestamp: { type: string, format: date-time }
        parameters: { type: object }
        ttlSeconds: { type: integer, minimum: 0, default: 300 }

  securitySchemes:
    mtls:
      type: X509
      description: "Mutual TLS — device client certificate authentication"
    tokenAuth:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer
      description: "JWT token for cloud-side MQTT clients"
```

### Step 4 — Configure QoS Levels

Apply QoS based on message criticality:

| Message Type | QoS | Rationale |
|-------------|-----|-----------|
| Periodic telemetry (temp, humidity) | 0 | Lossy OK — next reading corrects |
| Status change (online/offline) | 1 | Must arrive at least once |
| Device commands | 2 | Must arrive exactly once |
| High-frequency sensor stream | 0 | Bandwidth preservation |
| Firmware update trigger | 2 | Safety-critical, no duplicates |
| Billing/metering events | 2 | Financial accuracy required |
| Alert/alarm notifications | 1 | At-least-once is sufficient |

### Step 5 — Configure MQTT 5 Properties

When `mqtt_version` is `5.0`, add to message bindings:

```yaml
x-mqtt5-properties:
  # Payload format indicator
  contentType: "application/json"

  # Message expiry (TTL in seconds)
  messageExpiryInterval: 3600

  # Request-reply correlation
  responseTopic: "{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/commands/response"
  correlationData: "{requestId}"

  # Custom metadata routing
  userProperties:
    deviceType: "{type}"
    firmwareVersion: "{semver}"
    region: "{region}"
```

For MQTT 3.1.1, omit these properties and encode metadata in the payload body.

### Step 6 — Define Wildcard Subscriptions

Document subscription patterns for consumers:

```yaml
x-subscription-patterns:
  all-telemetry:
    filter: "{org}/{site}/devices/+/telemetry"
    description: "All devices at a site — single-level wildcard"
  all-site-data:
    filter: "{org}/{site}/#"
    description: "Everything from a site — multi-level wildcard"
  specific-sensor:
    filter: "{org}/+/devices/+/telemetry/temperature"
    description: "Temperature from any device at any site"
  shared-processing:
    filter: "$share/{groupName}/{org}/{site}/devices/+/telemetry"
    description: "MQTT 5 shared subscription — load-balanced consumers"
```

Wildcard rules:
- `+` matches exactly one topic level
- `#` matches zero or more levels (must be last)
- Never mix `#` with trailing levels
- Shared subscriptions: `$share/{group}/{filter}` (MQTT 5 only)

### Step 7 — Invoke Generator

```bash
cd {workspace}
python -m uptempo.schema.mqtt \
  --issue-id "{issue.identifier}" \
  --workspace "{workspace}" \
  --mqtt-version "{3.1.1|5.0}" \
  --domain "{domain}"
```

The generator (`src/uptempo/schema/mqtt.py`) implements `SchemaGenerator`:
- `generate(issue, workspace)` → writes files, returns `list[Path]`
- `validate(files)` → runs `asyncapi validate`, returns error list

### Step 8 — Validate

```bash
# Validate AsyncAPI document
npx @asyncapi/cli validate {workspace}/mqtt/{domain}-mqtt.yaml

# Validate JSON Schema payloads
npx ajv validate -s {schema_file} -d /dev/null --strict=true
```

Pass criteria:
- Zero errors from `asyncapi validate`
- All `$ref` pointers resolve
- Every channel has explicit `qos` in MQTT binding
- `lastWill` defined on server binding
- Retained messages only on status channels
- Topic hierarchy ≤ 7 levels deep

## Security Configuration

```yaml
x-mqtt-security:
  transport: TLS 1.3
  authentication:
    - method: client-certificate
      description: "X.509 mTLS for device identity"
    - method: username-password
      description: "Fallback for constrained devices"
  authorization:
    type: ACL
    rules:
      - client: "device-{deviceId}"
        publish: ["{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/telemetry",
                  "{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/status"]
        subscribe: ["{org}/{site}/devices/{deviceId}/commands/#"]
      - client: "cloud-service-*"
        publish: ["{org}/{site}/devices/+/commands/#"]
        subscribe: ["{org}/{site}/devices/#"]
```

## Error Handling

| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| MQTT version unspecified | Default to 5.0, set `x-mqtt-version-assumed: "5.0"` |
| QoS unspecified per channel | Default to QoS 1, document rationale in `x-qos-rationale` |
| No device types in issue | Generate generic `sensor` + `actuator` types, set `x-auto-derived: true` |
| Topic depth > 7 levels | Flatten hierarchy and emit warning in `x-topic-depth-warning` |
| `asyncapi validate` fails | Return errors to agent for correction, retry once |
| Mixed MQTT 3.1.1 / 5.0 clients | Generate 3.1.1-compatible base with 5.0 extensions in `x-mqtt5-*` |

## Collaboration Hooks

- **event-engineer**: Map MQTT messages ↔ internal Kafka/NATS events for cloud processing
- **api-architect**: Coordinate REST device management endpoints with MQTT topic provisioning
- **realtime-engineer**: Bridge MQTT telemetry → SSE/WebSocket for browser dashboards
- **schema-reviewer**: Submit AsyncAPI MQTT schemas for Phase 3 validation
